Coding Round
Online on Hackerearth
3 Questions of weightage: 20, 50, 50
Duration: 1.5 hours
1. Optimal use of two power resources:
Two power resources and their initial power capacity were given as input. At every step we
have to optimally choose between one of the resources. At every step capacity of chosen
resource gets reduced by 2 and that of the unchosen resource increases by 1 so you can only
choose a resource with capacity greater than 1. Repeat this until one of the power stations
capacity becomes zero.
Return the number of steps required if we use the resources optimally.
Sample input: 5, 3
Output: 6
It is solved by greedy approach by choosing the greater number at each step.
I passed all test cases.
2. Most similar string for a given query:
Given a list of strings and a query string, we have to find the string from the list which is most
similar or closest to the given query string. To do so we have to calculate the Levenshtein
distance ( minimum number of insert a character/delete character / replace character
operations to be performed on a string to convert the string to the given query). Return the
word with lowest Levenshtein distance. If two words have the same Levenshtein distance,
then the a lexicographically smaller word is the answer.
Finding the Levenshtein distance is a well known DP problem - Edit distance
I partially passed test cases for this problem.
3. Blacklink sorting:
Given a string array of webpage titles and an integer array of number of blacklinks on the
corresponding pages, we have to return the webpage titles in decreasing order of number of
blacklinks in them. If two pages contain same number of blacklinks then arrange them in order
of their index in the input array.
Output will be a list of strings.
I passed all test cases.
40 students were shortlisted for the offline interviews which were held on 9th August
2023 in TPO and unfortunately I wasn't one of them. But it merely ends here.

Interview Rounds
I wasn't one of the 40 people to get shortlisted so on the day of interviews, I was at IIT-Bombay
for a project I was working on and I get a call from the TPO informing me that I have been
shortlisted for DB interviews as I was in the waitlist and some students had to back off from
the interviews (big thanks to them💪 ). So I had to rush back to my house, change into my
formals and went for the interview.
Technical Round 1
The interview got started, he asked me to tell me about myself till my 10th standard,
without including the academic part, he explicitly asked me to exclude the academic part.
Later he asked me some situation based questions, core fundamentals related to OS and
COA. The round went on for 45-60 minutes.
This is a situation: A hacker is sitting in the college canteen and has access to the locations
of every phone inside the campus. Now we want to do something that will set the location
of all the devices in the TPO seminar hall, so how will we achieve this? 
I told him we’ll set up proxies on the devices and trip the location to the seminar hall, but
he said the hacker is smart too so he’ll know we’re doing this. Then I told him, we’ll gather
all the people here at the seminar hall, he said the hacker will find that people have
gathered here so he’ll know something’s wrong. The answer he gave was to gather all the
mobiles in the seminar hall instead of gathering people. 
Asked me about my internship. I did a research Internship at IIT-Bombay, I took a pen and
paper to explain it. Then asked me to elaborate on my projects.
Then he asked me to write a code on any application (but it should be valuable and like
something that we could use) in any language of my choice. So I first explained what
application I was writing a code on, wrote the code for encryption function of Caesar
Cipher.
He asked me if I knew size names like KB, MB etc. and asked me to arrange them in
increasing sequence. Answered it instantly.

Asked me to rank the storage devices in terms of speed. The devices were: Cache, RAM,
ROM, SSD, HDD. I answered this instantly. 
Now a question that, he thought was quite easy but I could not recall the concept and to
be honest, it was an easy question but I could not make it out. The question was to rank
the following terms in concentric circle sequence. Terms: Shell, Kernel, User, Hardware and
Application.
Since I was not aware of this, he asked me a similar question with a different terminology,
now the terms were: JAVA, JRE, JVM and JDK. I answered this correctly.
Then asked me about the OSI model in Computer Networks. I arranged all the 7 layers
correctly.
Now, he asked me to be the interviewer and ask him a technical question. I was quite
overwhelmed with this but he said you’ll have to ask me. So I asked him to list one or two
scenarios where Stack Overflow occurs. I played this very cleverly as I knew it might
backfire so I asked him something that I already knew. And now he asked me to answer
this exact question. So I told him the scenario of infinite loop, how the stack space will
eventually get filled. Later he told me one more scenario and explained it.
Later asked me if I knew interrupts. I asked me if he was talking about keyboard interrupts
and hardware interrupts. He said yes, so I explained him whatever I had learnt in OS. He
then explained in very detailed manner.
He then asked me about deadlocks and asked if I could describe a scenario where deadlock
condition occurs.
His last question was a scenario where he told me that there’s a computer having 512MB of
ram and Chrome is already running on it, consuming about 400MB ram and now I need to
run another application that consumes, say 200MB, so how will OS run it simultaneously? I
explained him the entire logic of virtual memory, how page files are created and
virtualization is achieved with the help of fragments. Tip: Try to explain stuff on paper.
There were 1-2 more questions but the day of interview was so long, it’s hard to recall each
and every thing but the interviewer sticked to the fundamentals and then asked me if I had
any questions for him, I asked him 2 questions.

Technical Round 2
As I was done with my 1st round, in like 5-10 minutes, I was immediately called up for the
2nd round.
Looking at my technical skills, he asked me the difference between MongoDB and
PostgreSQL.
He asked me about my internship, what I worked on, asked me to draw an architectural
design of the rule engine (where my work was), I drew the entire project in a flowchart and
explained what exactly happens in the rule engine, he asked me 2-3 follow up questions
and then was quite convinced. Tip: Please DO NOT LIE in your resume. They are very
experienced people so they’ll catch you if you lie, trust me.
As I was answering, he was taking a good look at my resume. I had a MERN stack project of
a bus ticket booking platform so he asked me where it was deployed, I told him it was done
locally and that I had not deployed it. He said it’s fine no issues.
He asked me if I knew Balanced Trees? I had heard about it but wasn't sure so I clearly told
him the same and he was okay with it. Please do not force an answer, only attempt if
you're sure.
Then he dived into DSA. Asked me a question. 
I asked him for some time and he was more than okay to let me work on it while looking
into my resume. I worked out a solution using circular linked list and maintaining node
pointers for person and knife. You can google the question to get a detailed solution.
Wrote the pseudocode and then he asked me 1-2 follow up questions and was convinced.
He had a very good look at my resume, said and I quote, “Rushil you have a very good
academic background, 10th, 12th and in engineering as well, why not go for Masters?”
Asked me who is the President of India? I answered it instantly.
Given inorder and preorder traversal build a binary tree from it.
https://leetcode.com/problems/construct-binary-tree-from-preorder-and-inorder-traversal/
Longest Palindromic Substring question (available on Leetcode). I first explained the naive
approach and then optimized it using Dynamic Programming. He was quite convinced after
3 DSA questions. https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-palindromic-substring/
Question: Given an integer n in a function, n denotes the number of people sitting on a round
table. Now, say for n=5, the first person has a knife, he kills his immediate right i.e. 2nd one
and passes the knife to the 3rd person. 3rd does the same, kills 4 and passes to 5, 5 kills 1 and
now since only 5 is remaining, return 5. He asked me what data structure will be used and
write the code for that function on paper.
Tip: This is one of the most commonly asked questions in interviews so if you come across
this, please have a well prepared answer. Also, if you really want the company, the answer to
this is straight up no. With a convincing explanation of course.

PROFESSIONAL FITNESS ROUND
After lunch, students were called up by names and we had to be ready for the interview.
This round was, in my opinion centered towards HR but kind of a test to see if we would be
a good fit for the company or not.
The interviewer seemed calm and experienced, asked me how my day was so far.
Now, the interviewer started off with some general questions. So he started off with my
internship, asked me to explain in absolute layman terms. Since he was not from a
technical background, he asked me questions about some technical terms that I
mentioned.
Then he asked me why Deutsche bank, what drives you here.
Asked me a question that, you’re from a technical background, he said why are you
applying for an investment bank and not some service based company. I told him that I had
contacts working at both these types of companies and also one contact that shifted from
service based to Deutsche bank and he told me it’s a greater exposure here and better
work environment. This was kind of unexpected so I had to put up a presentable answer.
Then he straight up asked, if you get an opportunity to work at a company like TCS and
Deutsche bank, which would you choose?
"What do you think your daily life will look like if you're working at Deutsche Bank?" I told
him my answer and he misunderstood a bit and said that I might be unfit for the role
they're hiring for. I cleared his misunderstanding and then he was fine with it.
Again the question of Masters, he asked me if I’ll be going for masters, again, I told him the
same answer that I had prepared.
Then he asked me if I had any questions, I asked me about the work life at Deutsche Bank,
their culture and work life balance etc. He elaborated in a very detailed manner and told
me how good it is to work at Deutsche bank. Asked him about recession.
This round went on for about 20-30 minutes and was mostly HR based fitness questions.

HR ROUND
After the professional fitness round, again students were called up one by one for the last
round. This was around 5 P.M and we were very exhausted. But of course, it was all worth
taking efforts for :)
The HR interview started with the interviewer asking me how the day was so far.
Then my introduction, she asked me to describe me what my day looks like, things I do. I
told her honestly.
She asked me to explain more about my internship. Again, I asked for a paper and drew the
whole flowchart. I told her that I'll also be working on it in my Final year so she asked me if
I'll still work there after college. Obviously, I said no.
Describe a big mistake that I had made and accepted, not academic related though. So, I
honestly told her the whole scenario.
Why I’d like to work at Deutsche bank?
She gave me a situation where I'm having a conflict with one of my colleague and asked me
how I'll resolve it.
Then she asked me if I’d apply in further college placements. Since Deutsche bank is a
dream company, I told her that we won’t be a part of placements anymore if we get
selected here.
Then she asked, if say a company comes that is a better opportunity than Deutsche,
possibly a better compensation, then would you regret it? I told her, first of all, for me, I
think, companies should not be arranged as dream and normal just on basis of the
compensation they offer but also organized by the reputation, history and work culture so
I told her, I have people working at Deutsche and they’ve suggested that it’s one of the
best companies to work at so no, absolutely zero regrets.
HR rounds are usually meant to see how you'll handle the non technical stuff at corporate
offices so be ready for scenario based questions.
Immensely grateful to VJTI and VJTI TPO for providing me this opportunity, years and years of
preparation finally paid off. And when they announced the results in the seminar hall itself, I
was one of the 26 candidates to be selected in Deutsche bank, a record-breaking placement for
VJTI TPO.
Special thanks to the 6 students that backed out of the process so that I could get an
opportunity!

Resources and Tips
Tips
 Be calm and composed for the interview, students tend to get nervous and get panicked,
resulting in a poor performance. Have some water if you want, settle in, it's just a
conversation with a person.
For preparation, please be consistent. This is the single most important thing that is
enough for you to get a dream placement. I had months of Leetcode daily streak before
landing this job. You'll have to constantly keep preparing without taking big breaks.
Always ask questions at the end of the interview. They'll ask you if you have any questions.
So please frame some questions that you could have a conversation on like, recession,
work culture at the company etc.
As you get shortlisted for the interview, ask your seniors about the process, questions etc.
If there are no seniors working at the company, connect people/alumni that are working
there on LinkedIn and ask them.
Do a well rounded research about the company before the interview, you should be having
a working knowledge about what the company does.
Remember, our college gives us opportunities that are very rare when it comes to
engineering colleges, so make sure you make the best out of it.
Lastly, always remember, it's just a process. You'll get through it if you're consistent and
smart.
All the very best to whoever is reading this doc, I wish you get your dream company! 🙌
THANK YOU
